pr.title: fix: Propagate query failures and bound snapshot archives
pr.body:
Deferred document encoding previously logged failures and returned successful queries containing only already-indexed vectors. A corruption regression reproduced this through five existing fallible APIs with both truncated and bit-flipped retained text.

`WarmCore::query`, `query_batch`, and `analyze_components` now return `Result`; dense-vector, knowledge, authenticated, federated-local and Node calls propagate errors. In-tree callers handle the intentional Rust API break. The regression covers eight query paths, unchanged durable state after failure, and successful recovery after cache repair.

Document-store contention still searches already-indexed vectors without waiting for catch-up; remote federated-peer failures retain their documented partial-result policy. This change does not introduce snapshot completeness under concurrent writes.

Validation: corruption/recovery regression; all-feature/all-target compilation and strict Clippy; 95 engine tests (one external-index diagnostic ignored); 20 encoder/ingest/reliability tests; security-sidecar recovery; 20 serial HTTP API tests; scoped formatting; and offline standalone ingest benchmark compilation pass. The benchmark's stale options initializer now uses existing defaults. The first parallel HTTP run had four response-deadline failures; logs are preserved, and serial success does not prove their cause. No deadlines or assertions were weakened. Reproduction evidence and limits are in `docs/research/technical-audit-20261029/REMEDIATION.md` and `raw-query-errors-20261031/`.

Windows CI also exposed a two-document snapshot transferring 1 GiB of unused journal capacity and exceeding the existing restore deadline. Format-4 snapshot exports now omit only verified zero padding beyond the active journal’s 64 MiB-aligned used boundary, including its end marker. Source snapshots and live files remain unchanged; older formats and nonzero tails retain their full lengths. All archive files use regular tar entries, including sparse auxiliary files, to preserve restore compatibility.

Snapshot validation: five core admin tests, six archive tests, all 13 serial operator tests, strict all-feature/all-target Clippy and scoped formatting passed. Boundary tests cover allocation limit−1/limit/limit+1, source preservation, nonzero tails, link rejection and vector recovery after extraction. The HTTP regression requires the small fixture archive to remain below 65 MiB. The failed Windows log and final local results are archived in `snapshot-padding-20261031/`; fresh cross-platform CI is required before merge. No timeout was relaxed.
